result.summary: This PR makes the bitcoin-wallet 'dump' command fail loudly and clean up its output file when writes or the final commit/close do not fully succeed, instead of silently reporting success on a truncated dump. It switches dump.cpp from std::ofstream to AutoFile, wraps the write path in a throw/catch pattern for cleaner control flow, and adds an AutoFile::Commit() plus DirectoryCommit() call to force data to disk before declaring success. A new functional test uses RLIMIT_FSIZE on POSIX to force a mid-write failure and checks that the tool exits nonzero, reports the error, and removes the partial dump file.
result.problem: Previously DumpWallet() only checked that the file could be opened; later write or close failures were ignored, so bitcoin-wallet could print the private-key warning and exit successfully while leaving behind a truncated, unusable dump file. Users relying on this dump as a backup would have no indication their backup was incomplete.

categories.name: wallet
categories.evidence: PR modifies src/wallet/dump.cpp, the wallet dump tool's core write logic, and carries the Wallet label.
categories.rationale: A wallet backup tool that can silently report success on a truncated dump is a real risk: a user relying on that dump for recovery would discover the problem only when trying to restore, per the PR description ('the tool could still return success... leaving a truncated dump file behind'). The added AutoFile Commit/DirectoryCommit further closes a durability gap where even a fully-written file could be lost on crash before fsync, per reviewer sedited and pablomartin4btc's detailed explanation. This is not a headline security bug but touches backup integrity, which the wallet category treats as high priority just below fund-loss bugs.

uncertainties: No linked GitHub issue confirms a user actually hit a truncated dump in practice; severity assessment relies on the described failure mode being plausible and reviewer corroboration.
Exact likelihood of RLIMIT_FSIZE-style failures occurring in real deployments (disk full, quota limits) is not quantified in the discussion.
result.card: This PR fixes bitcoin-wallet's 'dump' command so it fails and removes the partial output file when writing or committing the dump does not fully succeed, instead of silently reporting success on a truncated file. It matters because a wallet dump is often used as a backup, and a truncated dump masquerading as successful could leave a user without a real backup, discovered only during a recovery attempt. The PR evolved through review from a simple write-check fix to using AutoFile with Commit()/DirectoryCommit() for real fsync-level durability, per reviewer sedited's suggestion, closing an even subtler crash-durability gap identified by pablomartin4btc. Reviewer pablomartin4btc gave Approach ACK then a full ACK on the final commit with a detailed technical rationale, and no objections remain; earlier style nits from maflcko were resolved by rewrite. A minor follow-up (surfacing errno detail in AutoFile throw sites) was explicitly split into a separate PR (#36210) and does not block this one.
